terms.gloss: an appointment, an arrangement to meet
evidence: Cic. Fam. 7.4: sī quod cōnstitūtum cum podagrā habēs (Lewis & Short s.v. cōnstituō)
terms.comment: The neuter of cōnstitūtus, “something agreed”. To have an appointment with someone is cōnstitūtum habēre cum aliquō.

terms.gloss: keep an appointment, come at the agreed time
evidence: Varr. RR 2.5.1; Cic. Caecin. 33 (Lewis & Short s.v. cōnstituō)

phrases.latin: sī quod cōnstitūtum cum podagrā habēs, fac ut in alium diem differās
phrases.english: if you have an appointment with your gout, put it off to another day
to have a date with someone

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 93, 300.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
